Minimal nonparametric regression demo data (oracle m and Y only)

Source: R/demo-data-npr.R
np_demo_data.Rd

Generates a simple nonparametric regression dataset with features \(X\) and response \(Y = m(X) + \epsilon\), returning the oracle regression function \(m(x)\). This is designed for experimenting with the Y-only singleton score score_np_y().

Usage

np_demo_data(
  n = 200,
  p = 2,
  design = c("linear", "sinusoidal", "bump", "constant"),
  sigma = 0.5,
  seed = NULL,
  x0 = NULL,
  inject = NULL,
  idx_inject = 3L
)

Arguments

n

Integer; sample size.

p

Integer; number of features in \(X\).

design

Character; one of "linear", "sinusoidal", "bump", "constant".

sigma

Noise standard deviation in \(Y\).

seed

Optional integer seed, used locally without changing the caller's RNG state. NULL uses the current stream.

x0

Optional target point in \(\mathbb{R}^p\) (defaults to the zero vector).

inject

Optional, one of NULL, "na", "inf"; if provided, inject a single non-finite value into Y at idx_inject (useful for tests).

idx_inject

Integer index at which to inject NA/Inf (default 3).

Value

A list with:

  • data: data.frame with columns X1..Xp, Y, and m_oracle (=\(m(X)\)).

  • x0: the target point used.

  • truth: list with closure m_fn(x) for evaluating \(m(x)\) at new \(X\).

  • m_x0: the true \(m(x_0)\).

Examples

demo <- np_demo_data(n = 200, p = 2, design = "sinusoidal", seed = 1)
head(demo$data)
#>           X1         X2           Y   m_oracle
#> 1 -0.6264538  0.4094018  0.28598513 -0.2512354
#> 2  0.1836433  1.6888733  1.75220705  0.8043797
#> 3 -0.8356286  1.5865884 -0.04304208  0.2584566
#> 4  1.5952808 -0.3309078  0.33179122  0.5272251
#> 5  0.3295078 -2.2852355  1.25925301  1.4673640
#> 6 -0.8204684  2.4976616  1.00601700  1.1938457
demo$m_x0
#> [1] 0
